verdict: READY TO MERGE - 21 of 24 findings resolved, 3 bubbled
strengths: todo_id pattern is equivalent to ids.py ID_RE (same alphabet, 4 characters, lookaheads for one digit and one letter), and the description's alphabet and exclusions (no 0, 1, i, l, o) match ALPHABET.
legacy_todo_id kept as a separate def used only for legacy_ids.map keys, so old ids never validate as live ids; T1 filters only their pattern errors, leaving other errors intact.

New retired_ids, legacy_ids and split_ids properties are optional and closed (additionalProperties false), so existing catalogs still validate; split_ids/retired_ids/legacy_ids prose agrees with the T6 rules and migrate.py behavior.
Cross-record rule list in the description (T6-T10, unchecked fields) matches the rule code and schemas/README.md.

The id draw tests use a scripted rng (Scripted) to prove deterministically that new_id, add_items and split_item redraw past retired, live and original ids, instead of relying on chance with a real rng.
test_todo_catalog_schema.py checks the schema's id pattern against is_id over one shared list of good and bad codes, so the JSON Schema and the Python validator cannot drift apart unnoticed.

The migrate tests cover the failure paths behaviorally: git grep failing, a locked file write followed by a rerun that finishes from the stored map, a project schema that rejects the new ids, non-UTF-8 files and CRLF preservation, each asserting that the catalog bytes are untouched.

test_operations_refuse_a_legacy_catalog drives retire, split, refresh and add through the real driver against the legacy fixture, and asserts the exit code, the 'problem: <op>:' prefix and that the catalog bytes did not change.
MUST_EXIT_ZERO in test_root_separation.py now includes the todo_sync retire, split, refresh and migrate-ids cases, so a refusal can no longer pass the outside-the-project snapshot check vacuously.
The rewritten tests check byte-level non-mutation of companions and history records (_bytes before and after) instead of only parsed content, which fits the new 'list, never rewrite' contract.
No mock-chain wiring tests: every monkeypatch is fault injection on a real collaborator (subprocess.run, write_file, the gh fake), and the outcome is asserted on files or reports.
migrate seeds each draw from sha256(old id, title), so a dry run, its real run and two checkouts agree on the new ids without storing state.
migrate refuses on a rejecting project schema and on git grep failure before any write, and a partial write failure is recoverable by rerunning through the stored legacy_ids map.
Moving TodoSyncError to errors.py breaks the import cycle cleanly while __init__ still re-exports it.
_rewrite_text and dump_like preserve line endings, BOM-free strict UTF-8 and indentation, and undecodable files are reported as skipped rather than corrupted.
resolve_ids triages retired, split and legacy ids into specific, joined problem messages instead of a bare 'no such item'.
A failed reference scan degrades to scan_error after the catalog write instead of failing the whole retire or split.

The todo-editor agent's description of report lines matches the script output exactly: 'dangling: <where> names retired <id>' (retire.py:117, :187), 'names split <orig> (parts <a>, <b>)' (reshape.py:376) and 'reference scan failed:' (retire.py:329, reshape.py:592).

The history-folder list in the agent and the todo-edit skill (plans, reviews, commit_messages, summaries, scratch, planning prefixes, snapshots) matches retire.history_paths (retire.py:219-229) item for item.
The README's migrate-ids paragraph puts the risky steps in order: update the project schema and every install first, then a dry run; and it says why (an older harness renumbers stable ids back).
The agent's split step warns that dry-run part ids are provisional and must come from the real run's report, which matches reshape.DRAW_NOTE; a contract test pins it (B7).
The plan's id-space arithmetic is right: 31^4 - 23^4 - 8^4 = 639584, and the schema pattern's character classes give exactly the 23 letters and 8 digits in the documented alphabet.
The harness row in the release table (0.65.0) matches plugins/harness/.claude-plugin/plugin.json at the head.
Every example id in the skill and agent (`k7qf`, `todo-2a2a`, `todo-m3x9`) is valid under `ids.ALPHABET` and the digit-plus-letter rule, so the examples do not contradict the format they teach.
Step 3's history-folder list (plans, reviews, commit_messages, summaries, scratch, planning prefixes, snapshots) matches `retire.history_paths` exactly, and the agent's Rules repeat the same list.

Skill and agent agree on the migrate-ids stop: the skill says the agent relays the refusal and the developer runs the switch, and the agent's Stop conditions spell out both commands and forbid running it; the contract test pins both sides.
No orphan rank-tied wording survives in either skill package: no `TODO-NNN` normalization, no renumbering, and sync-gh-todo's `add` line now says it inserts and ranks.

The id design is complete end to end. ids.py is the single source for the format, the draw, canonicalization, `mentions` and `resolve_ids`, and retire, reshape, migrate, rules_todo, add_todo.py and issues.py all import it rather than keeping their own regexes.

migrate-ids is built for a partial failure. A git grep failure and a project-schema rejection both refuse before any write. The catalog is written first, carrying the full map. A failed file write names every file not written, and a rerun finishes through the stored `legacy_ids` map. Tests cover each path (test_a_failed_file_write_leaves_the_map_for_a_rerun, test_rerun_applies_the_stored_map_to_live_files).

Seeding each migration draw from sha256(old id, title) makes the dry run and the real run agree on the ids, which the tests check (test_migration_ids_are_reproducible). add and split keep the random draw and print a provisional-ids note on a dry run.

resolve_ids turns a stale reference into an answer, not just 'unknown': an old TODO-NNN reports what the map says it meant and its date, a split id names its parts, and a retired id says it was retired.

T1 and T6 report a legacy catalog as one actionable migrate-ids finding (plus the duplicates migrate-ids needs cleared) instead of a pattern error per id. retire, split, add, refresh, add-todo and untracked all refuse it before doing any work, so gh and agent dispatch never run.

other_references drops the history folders in Python instead of passing exclude pathspecs, which avoids the Windows command-line limit. A failed scan becomes a reported `scan_error`, not a silent empty list.

The tests are behavioral throughout. They run real git projects through make_project and drive the CLI as a subprocess, and the only seams are fault injections (subprocess.run raising OSError, write_file failing), never stubs of the code under test. MUST_EXIT_ZERO now covers retire, split, refresh and migrate-ids, so a refusal can no longer pass the root-separation check vacuously.
The legacy fixture is a byte-identical copy of the base min fixture, and _todo_helpers spells TodoCatalog.legacy.json out in code, so tools/select_tests.py maps fixture changes to their readers.
The plan records each decision with its rejected options, and the repository's own switch is deferred until after the release, with the needed `--exclude plugins --exclude tests` written down.

One module (todo_sync/ids.py) owns the id format, the generator, resolution and the legacy guard; the schema pattern, T6, README.md:404-406 and schemas/README.md:182 all describe the same 31-character alphabet with a digit and a letter.

The schema description, schemas/README.md:184 and t6_ids_and_ranks list the same cross-record rules (unique, not retired, split_ids keys retired, parts live or retired), so docs and code agree on what T6 checks.
The legacy refusal sits at the shared load_catalog chokepoint plus the add-todo and untracked pre-dispatch checks, so no write path can renumber a stable catalog or act on a legacy one.

Prose contract tests (test_todo_stable_id_prose.py, the todo-edit and sync-gh-todo contract tests) pin the README and skill text against renumbering language, keeping docs in lockstep with the behavior change.

plugin.json and docs/RELEASES/v0.7.0.md agree on harness 0.65.0, and the PIP records D14 deferring this repository's own catalog switch until the release ships, matching the README's install-first ordering.

important.name: README migrate-ids paragraph omits that it rewrites every live file in the repository
important.summary:
README.md:422-431 says migrate-ids keeps the map in legacy_ids and leaves history as written, and that --exclude skips a path, but never says what the run writes outside the catalog. The code (migrate.py:273-290 live_files, todo_sync.py:68-79 docstring, plan decision D13) rewrites the research catalog, the stubs and every tracked or untracked text file git grep finds naming TODO-NNN, source code and tests included; this repository's own deferred switch needs --exclude plugins --exclude tests for that reason (ActionPlan deferred_to_future_plans). A developer reading only the README cannot tell what --exclude is excluding from, or that files outside docs change. The same paragraph's history list (plans, reviews, snapshots, commit messages, PR summaries) also leaves out artifacts.scratch and each artifacts.planning_prefixes entry, which history_paths (retire.py:219-229) skips.

Also (docs): README.md:430 says 'Until the catalog is migrated, `retire`, `split`, `refresh` and `add` refuse'. ENT-1 also makes `todo_sync.py untracked` refuse (issues.py:123 `ids.require_stable(src.todo.data, "untracked")`) and `add_todo.py row` refuse (add_todo.py:68). Those are the first commands `/harness:sync-gh-todo` and `/harness:add-todo` run, and the README describes both flows a few lines below. A reader going by this list would not expect sync-gh-todo to stop at its first step. The v0.7.0 notes name both skills correctly.

Also (system_shape): issues.find_untracked (issues.py:118-124) now refuses a legacy catalog with 'untracked: <MIGRATE_HINT>', and the release notes (docs/RELEASES/v0.7.0.md:18-24) say sync-gh-todo refuses. But the docs that enumerate the refusals name only add, retire, split and refresh: README.md:430-431 and the todo_sync.py module docstring (todo_sync.py:82-84); the untracked section of that docstring (todo_sync.py:48-56) lists only the gh refusals, and find_untracked's own docstring is silent. README.md:431 also says check reports one T6 finding, while t6_ids_and_ranks (rules_todo.py:184-200) adds the duplicate-id findings, as schemas/README.md:184 correctly states.
fix: In README.md:423-425 add one sentence: the run rewrites every live file that names an old id (the research catalog, the stubs and each tracked or untracked text file git grep finds, source and tests included), minus the catalog schema, the history folders and each --exclude; the dry run lists those files first.
In the same paragraph list the full history set: plans, reviews, commit messages, summaries, scratch, each planning prefix and the snapshots.

Rewrite the sentence as: 'Until the catalog is migrated, `retire`, `split`, `refresh`, `add` and `untracked` refuse (so `/harness:add-todo` and `/harness:sync-gh-todo` stop before any dispatch), and `check` reports one T6 finding that names `migrate-ids`.'

Add untracked to the refusal lists in README.md:430 and todo_sync.py:83, add 'or the catalog still holds TODO-NNN ids (naming migrate-ids)' to the untracked section at todo_sync.py:55-56, and append 'plus any duplicate-id findings' to README.md:431.

important.name: A comma-joined id list the skill documents is refused by the script
important.summary:
todo-edit SKILL.md:23 accepts `--retire` ids 'comma- or space-separated', and :27 and :45 tell the session to pass them as typed because the script canonicalizes them. The agent runs `TS retire <ids>` (todo-editor.md:75). For `--retire k7qf,2a2a` (no space), argv holds one token, 'k7qf,2a2a'. `ids._clean` strips only one trailing ',' or ';', so `canonical` returns None, `_legacy_id` does not match, and `resolve_ids` raises "not a TODO id: 'k7qf,2a2a'". The agent's stop conditions then end the run. Before this PR the session normalized each id itself, so this documented input worked; now it fails closed.

Also (skill_package): Step 1's table accepts `--retire` ids that are comma- or space-separated (and the argument-hint reads `ID[, ID ...]`), but line 27 now says to pass each id as typed, and the prompt's `Ids:` line carries them as typed. The agent runs `TS retire <ids>`; `todo_sync.py retire` takes `ids` with nargs='+', and `ids.canonical` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/ids.py:69-79) strips only one trailing `,` or `;` per argv token. Input written as `--retire k7qf,todo-2a2a` (comma, no space) reaches the script as the single token `k7qf,todo-2a2a`, which `_triage` classes as malformed, so the run stops with `not a TODO id: 'k7qf,todo-2a2a'`. The old skill normalized each id and so split the list; the new text dropped that split without the script taking it over. The refusal is safe (nothing is written), but a documented input form fails every time.

Also (skill_package): Line 27-29 says the script 'canonicalizes it ..., names the item an old rank-tied id meant as of the migration, and refuses a retired, split or unknown id'. The list of refusals leaves out the rank-tied form, so a reader takes `TODO-007` / `7` as accepted and resolved through `legacy_ids`. In `ids._triage` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/todo_sync/ids.py:132-144) a rank-tied id is a `note` problem, and `resolve_ids` raises on any problem: the old id is refused, the note only names what it meant.

Also (skill_package): Line 19 keeps 'Free text after the ids with no `--` token is read as guidance too'. Under the old text an id was numeric (`TODO-007`, `007`, `7`), so the boundary was obvious; now ids are passed as typed with no shape stated beyond `todo-k7qf` / `k7qf`, so the session has no stated test for whether a token like `fix2` or `retire` is an id or the start of guidance. A wrong cut either sends guidance words to the script (a malformed-id refusal) or drops an id into Guidance.

Also (skill_package): Line 29 runs to about 170 characters, joining the new sentence's tail to the old `--delete-retired` sentence; every other prose line in the file wraps near 110.
fix: In `resolve_ids` (ids.py:157-174), split each raw on `[,;\s]+` and drop empty pieces before `_triage`, so 'k7qf,2a2a' and 'k7qf, 2a2a' resolve alike. Add a case to tests/lib/test_todo_sync_ids.py::test_canonical_accepts_any_case_and_a_bare_code or a new resolve test.
Alternatively, have SKILL.md:27/:45 and todo-editor.md:75 tell the session and agent to split the typed list into separate arguments, and pin that with a contract test.
In Step 1, say the session splits the ids at commas and whitespace and passes each piece as typed, joined with `, ` on the `Ids:` line (e.g. `Ids: k7qf, todo-2a2a`), so every argv token holds one id.
Or have the script split each `retire` argv token on `,` before `resolve_ids` (and pin it in tests/scripts), keeping the skill's pass-through rule as written.

Reword to: 'the script canonicalizes it (a trailing comma included) and refuses, with the reason, a retired, split or unknown id, or an old rank-tied id (naming the item it meant as of the migration).'
State the shape in Step 1: an id token is `todo-` plus four characters, or the four characters alone, holding at least one digit and one letter; the first token that is neither starts the guidance.
Rewrap lines 27-32 at 110 columns.

minor.name: todo-editor looks up ids by their canonical form, but ids arrive as typed and the script only canonicalizes later
minor.summary:
The agent's catalog lookup (todo-editor.md:47-48) greps for `"id": "todo-k7qf"`. The next sentence says ids 'may arrive in any case or as a bare code; the script canonicalizes them'. The todo-edit skill passes ids as typed (SKILL.md:27, 45), so the description's own example sends `Ids: k7qf, todo-2a2a` (line 19). Retire step 1 (:72) and split step 1 (:111) read the item before any script runs, so a literal Grep for `"id": "k7qf"` or `"id": "K7QF"` finds nothing. The split spec path `split-<id>.json` (:115) takes whatever form arrived. The agent has to work out the canonical form on its own, and the prose does not say how.

Also (overall): todo-editor.md:47-48 tells the agent to Grep for `"id": "todo-k7qf"` and says ids 'may arrive in any case or as a bare code; the script canonicalizes them'. The split flow reads the item before any script runs (step 1) and names the spec file `split-<id>.json` (:115). An Ids line of `K7QF` or `k7qf,` therefore leads to a case-sensitive Grep miss on `"todo-K7QF"`, or a file name like `split-k7qf,.json`. The script's canonicalization never reaches those agent-side steps.

Also (system_shape): todo-editor.md:47-49 tells the agent to Grep for '"id": "todo-k7qf"' and, in the same bullet, that ids may arrive in any case or as a bare code because the script canonicalizes them. Retire step 1 (:72) and split step 1 (:111) read the item before any script runs, so an id typed as K7QF or k7qf (the todo-edit SKILL.md:23 example) gives a Grep that misses the lowercase, prefixed id stored in the catalog.
fix: In the Environment bullet, add: 'Before any lookup or file name, write each id in its canonical form: lower-case, with `todo-` added when missing (`K7QF` -> `todo-k7qf`).'
Or tell retire and split to run the dry run first and take the canonical ids from its first line (`would retire todo-k7qf, ...` / `would split todo-m3x9 into ...`) before reading the items.
In todo-editor.md:47-48 and :115, tell the agent to canonicalize the id itself before its Grep and the spec file name: lower-case it, drop a trailing ',' or ';', and prefix `todo-` when missing.

In todo-editor.md:47-48 say to Grep for the canonical form: lowercase the id and add the todo- prefix when it is a bare code (or Grep case-insensitively for the bare code), before reading around the hit.

minor.name: taken_ids ignores ids the catalog still records in legacy_ids and split_ids
minor.summary: taken_ids returns live item ids plus retired_ids only. An item deleted by hand (not through retire) leaves its id in legacy_ids.map values or split_ids parts but outside both sets, so add or split can redraw it; resolve_ids then reports 'TODO-012 ... meant todo-xxxx (<unrelated new title>)' and split_ids names a part that is now a different item, contradicting the schema's 'a retired id is never reused' intent. T6 does not flag legacy map values that are neither live nor retired, so nothing surfaces the gap.
fix: Add the string values of legacy_ids.map and the keys and parts of split_ids to the set taken_ids returns.
Or add a T6 check that every legacy_ids.map value is a live item or in retired_ids.

minor.name: migrate imports private helpers _companions and _under from retire
minor.summary: migrate.py imports the underscore-private _companions and _under across modules; they are now shared API of retire.py, so the leading underscore misstates their contract and a later private refactor of retire breaks migrate silently.
fix: Rename them companions and under_any (or similar public names) in retire.py and update retire.py and migrate.py call sites.

minor.name: migrate-ids --exclude silently ignores absolute or cwd-relative paths
minor.summary: live_files compares each --exclude value, after posix() (backslashes and a leading ./ only), as a prefix of the project-relative paths git grep prints from the project root. An absolute path (E:/repo/vendor) or a path relative to a working directory below the root (cwd docs/, --exclude old for docs/old) never matches, so the exclusion is a no-op and a real run rewrites the files the person meant to keep. Nothing reports that an --exclude matched no candidate.
fix: Resolve each --exclude against the working directory, take it relative_to(cfg.project_root) and refuse (TodoSyncError) one that lies outside the root; keep the component-prefix match on the result.
Alternatively, report each --exclude that matched no candidate as an 'exclude matched nothing:' line in summary_lines so a dry run exposes the typo.

minor.name: _ID_RECORDS and the catalog mention walker are duplicated in retire and reshape
minor.summary: retire.py:28 and reshape.py:45 each define the same `_ID_RECORDS` frozenset. `_dangling` (retire.py:111-126) and `_split_flags` (reshape.py:379-395) repeat the same walk: items under `items/<id>`, the id records skipped, `todo_ids.mentions` on each string. Only the note text differs. A fourth id record added later must be added in both places or one scan starts flagging it.
fix: Keep one `mention_paths(data, ids, note)` helper and the `_ID_RECORDS` constant in retire.py (reshape already imports from retire). Have both `_dangling` and `_split_flags` call it.

minor.name: add_items and refresh_items skip the legacy guard their siblings apply
minor.summary: `split_item` (reshape.py:78) and `retire_items` (retire.py:50) call `todo_ids.require_stable`, and their docstrings list the legacy refusal. The pure `add_items` (reshape.py:113-131) and `refresh_items` (:95-100) do not. On a `TODO-NNN` catalog, `add_items` builds a mixed catalog: a stable-id item among legacy ids. Only `_apply`'s `load_catalog` keeps the driver safe, so a library caller of the pure function gets no refusal.
fix: Call `todo_ids.require_stable(catalog, "add")` at the top of `add_items` and `todo_ids.require_stable(catalog, "refresh")` in `refresh_items`, and add the Raises line to each docstring.

minor.name: write_edits keeps a dead edits parameter and a stale docstring

The `edits` parameter and its loop in `write_edits` (retire.py:212-216) are dead, and the docstring 'then each rewritten companion' describes writes that no longer happen. `_companions` (retire.py:289-290) still says the companions are 'files whose TODO ids follow the catalog', which stopped being true when id rewrites were removed. tests/lib/test_todo_sync_file_issue.py:156 patches `write_edits` with `*args`, so dropping the parameter breaks nothing.

Also (system_shape): retire.write_edits (retire.py:212-216) is documented as 'Write the catalog atomically, then each rewritten companion', while the module docstring (retire.py:1-9) and every caller (retire.py:182, reshape.py:555) now write only the catalog and pass edits={}. The edits parameter has no production use left; the only other consumer is the test stub that swaps reshape.write_edits (tests/lib/test_todo_sync_file_issue.py:159).
fix: Drop the edits parameter and its loop, update the docstring to 'Write the catalog atomically', and update both callers (tests/lib/test_todo_sync_file_issue.py monkeypatches reshape.write_edits by name, so keep the function name).

Reduce `write_edits` to `(cfg, catalog_text)` writing only the catalog. Update its docstring and the two callers, and reword the `_companions` docstring to 'the research catalog and the stubs, scanned for mentions of a retired or split id (and rewritten only by migrate-ids)'.
Drop the edits parameter (and its loop) from write_edits, update both callers and the test stub's signature, and change the docstring to 'Write the catalog atomically'.
Keep the signature and change the docstring to say callers pass {} since ids became stable, so the module reads consistently.

minor.name: schemas README says legacy_ids is written once, but a migrate-ids rerun extends the map
minor.summary:
plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:181 describes `legacy_ids` as 'written once by `todo_sync.py migrate-ids`'. The code and decision D12 say otherwise: migrate.py:73 sets `data["legacy_ids"] = {"migrated": migrated, "map": {**known, **mapping}}`, so a rerun on a catalog that gained `TODO-NNN` items (for example from a branch merged after the switch) adds new entries to the stored map. A reader who treats the record as write-once would not expect it to change.

Also (system_shape): plugins/harness/schemas/README.md:180 describes legacy_ids as 'written once by todo_sync.py migrate-ids'. migrate_catalog (migrate.py:66-73) rewrites legacy_ids on every rerun, adding new legacy ids to the stored map (plan D12, todo_sync.py:76-78), so the record is not write-once.
fix: Replace 'written once by `todo_sync.py migrate-ids`' with 'written by `todo_sync.py migrate-ids`; a rerun adds new legacy ids and never changes a stored entry'.
Reword to 'written by todo_sync.py migrate-ids; a rerun adds new legacy ids to the map and keeps the first migrated date'.

minor.name: Schema description omits duplicate-id findings on a legacy catalog
minor.summary: The top-level description says a catalog with rank-tied TODO-NNN ids 'gets one T6 finding naming todo_sync.py migrate-ids'. t6_ids_and_ranks returns the migrate finding plus every duplicate-id finding for such a catalog (rules_todo.py:193-196), and schemas/README.md already says '(plus any duplicate ids)'. The schema prose is the only copy that claims exactly one.
fix: Reword to 'gets one T6 finding naming todo_sync.py migrate-ids, plus any duplicate-id findings', matching schemas/README.md.

minor.name: Shared min fixture still says ids are reproducible from the item fields
minor.summary: TodoCatalog.min.json ranking_method.notes still ends 'so ids and ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone.' (line 58). Under stable ids that sentence is false, and the PR changed the starter catalog to say 'ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone; ids never change', with test_todo_sync_scaffold.py:52 asserting the old phrase is gone from it. Every lib and script test copies this fixture, so the stale contract text ships in every test project and in any snapshot rendered from it. The legacy fixture keeps the old wording on purpose, since it models a catalog from before the switch.
fix: Replace the last sentence of ranking_method.notes in tests/fixtures/todo_sync/TodoCatalog.min.json with the starter wording from scaffold.py:67 ('... so ranks are reproducible from the item fields alone; ids never change.').

Move `Scripted` into tests/lib/_todo_helpers.py and import it in the three test files.

minor.name: is_id positive checks repeated in every parametrized case
minor.summary: test_is_id_rejects_words_numbers_lookalikes_and_case (tests/lib/test_todo_sync_ids.py:59-64) is parametrized over 14 rejected strings, and every case also asserts the same three accepted ids. test_canonical_accepts_any_case_and_a_bare_code (lines 67-70) has the same pattern with its three None checks. fix: Replace the inline slice at line 71 with section = _section(body, '## delete-retired').

minor.name: README renumber ban covers the whole README, not the TODO text
minor.summary:
test_readme_todo_text_never_renumbers (tests/skills/test_todo_stable_id_prose.py:17-20) and the module docstring scope the check to the README's TODO sync text. The code instead searches every line of README.md for /[Rr]enumber/. The README also documents plans, parallel2, bookmarks and PR tooling, so a legitimate 'renumber' anywhere else (plan or lane numbering, for example) fails a test about TODO ids, and the failure message points at the wrong feature.

Also (overall): `test_readme_todo_text_never_renumbers` (tests/skills/test_todo_stable_id_prose.py:17-20) fails on any 'renumber' anywhere in README.md. The README covers every plugin, so a later unrelated sentence would fail this TODO guard. An example is commit-block renumbering, which branch-commit-msg and amend-commit-msg do. The test name promises a narrower check than it makes.
fix: Limit the search to the TODO paragraphs, as test_readme_documents_migrate_ids already does: filter _paragraphs() to those naming todo_sync.py, RepoToDo or TODO, then assert no renumber hit in them.
Keep the global scan, but rename the test and update the docstring to state that the whole README is banned from saying 'renumber'.

Limit the scan to the TODO section, for example the paragraphs naming `todo_sync.py`, `todo-edit`, `add-todo` or `sync-gh-todo`, the way `test_readme_documents_migrate_ids` already filters paragraphs.
